prompt:
Create ONE original game-art PNG sprite sheet with a genuine transparent RGBA background, exactly FOUR SEPARATE ASH-MOTH SWARM STATES arranged in a strict 2 columns by 2 rows grid. This is original art for ASHVEIL, a bleak, quiet ash-covered survival world. This is NOT a painted scene, not an illustration with a background, not a chart and not animation in-betweens. No reference images. Do not imitate or copy any existing game's pixels.

STYLE AND SCALE: meticulous small-scale hand-clustered pixel art, hard-edged deliberate pixel clusters, subdued charcoal, soot-gray, warm ash-gray and bone-silver highlights. Every visible insect is a TINY moth with one short dark body, a paired set of folded or spread powdery gray wings and only subtle antennae. Many small individuals create each colony silhouette. Clearly varied wing openings and body headings, small speck-like distant insects. Never one giant central moth, no faces, no humanoids, no large butterflies, no fantasy eyes. No opaque black/white/checkerboard background, no atmospheric gray wash behind the insects. Transparent gaps must stay genuinely empty. Do not paint loose dust, smoke, stars or sparks as filler: visible marks should belong to insects.

LAYOUT: four fully isolated groups, one group per quadrant, generous empty transparent margins and a broad completely transparent cross-shaped gutter between groups. Keep every insect well inside its own quadrant, at least one moth-width from every group boundary; no insect touches the canvas edge. Each full group occupies only about 55-60 percent of the width and height of its quadrant, so all antennae and wings fit with ample safety margin. No boxes, dividers, words, labels, numbers, arrows, watermarks, ground planes, shadows, lights, lanterns, torches, candles, furniture, characters, vegetation or game tiles.

TOP LEFT — LOOSE RESTLESS SWARM: a loose shallow horizontal cloud of tiny ash moths, substantial clear spaces between the insects, calm irregular spacing and several natural wing angles, empty gaps through the group. About twenty-five individually readable tiny moth marks; this is only visual sampling, not a literal biological population count.
TOP RIGHT — DENSE LIGHT-ATTRACTED SWARM: clearly denser, roughly oval cloud of many tiny ash moths, loose outer edge and compact interior, subtly curling around a SMALL EMPTY CENTRAL OPENING. The moths are attracted toward an off-art source but NO actual lamp, light source, emitted glow, halo, circular outline or luminous particle is drawn. This state has roughly twice the visible insect marks of the loose group, with many tiny ash-gray wings still readable.
BOTTOM LEFT — MOVING SWARM: a broad asymmetric stream of tiny ash moths tending toward the right, with a rounded leading group and a sparse trailing edge. Wings naturally alternate raised, half-open and down between DIFFERENT INDIVIDUAL insects; no pasted rows, no motion streaks, no arrows. This is ONE static movement-state illustration, not a claimed flight-cycle sequence.
BOTTOM RIGHT — DISPERSING SWARM: a visibly thinning, irregular broken cloud with tiny moths oriented in several outward directions, a larger empty middle and a few smaller outer insects still safely inside the quadrant. No explosion, attack, gore, dust blast or magic. The mood is quiet ecological behavior.

Maintain the SAME tiny gray moth species, body scale, palette and amount of pixel detail in all four quadrants. Readable swarm shapes at small game scale, NOT enlarged portrait insects. Four original colony-state source regions in one PNG, with no duplicates or mirrored replacement groups.
